visual_thesis: AI delegation belongs on verifiable tasks while people retain judgment and accountability.
mechanism_metaphor: A bold flat matte-print branching composition. A single Task junction near the top divides into asymmetric interlocking branches: broad AI-assisted verifiable work on the left and an upright named responsibility branch on the right. No document cards, plaques, badges, bevels, sculpture or faux machine. The single arrow from the Task junction port at (600,220) goes to the verifiable-work branch port at (370,290), clear of all text. Other branches are nondirectional structural ties, not arrows. Show craft refinement, observable checks and feedback on the left using actual labeled typographic states; judgment, accountability and relationship work remain on the right. A small paired evidence footing carries source survey/guideline counts; these self-report counts cannot become quality outcome claims. All unused broad shapes remain solid and blank. The limiting note is independent at the lower edge, fully inset.

Story: Developers turn AI responsibility into task-level operating rules
Full published story: Microsoft researchers surveyed 860 developers to derive 35 guidelines for using AI across software work, then validated them with 258 developers at Microsoft, GitHub and Pfizer. Ninety-two percent found the guidance clear and 89% wanted to adopt it. These are self-reported judgments from three organizations, not measured changes in quality or safety.
Reader action: Turn one team policy into task-level operating rules: delegate work that has observable checks, keep judgment and accountability named, and review the rule after defects, handoffs or relationship-heavy work expose a mismatch.
